tagline: A lakeside town on Songkhla Lake — Khao Ok Thalu mountain, red lotus blooms at Thale Noi, rice fields with water buffalo, and the home of shadow puppetry and Manora dance
introHtml:
Phatthalung is a small southern province tucked between the Banthat mountain range and Songkhla Lake. People picture it through Khao Ok Thalu, the mountain with a hole punched through its middle that stands as the town's backdrop, through Thale Noi where red lotus cover the water at dawn, and through green rice fields with buffalo grazing along the lake. It's a slow-paced town where everyday local life is still easy to see.

This is one of the South's best-known homes of nang talung shadow puppetry and Manora dance, with old markets and wooden houses in town to wander. The food is bold southern fare — khao yam, gaeng tai pla, and khanom jeen. If you like nature, you can head up the Banthat range to the waterfalls, take a boat to watch the birds at Thale Noi, or sit by the water at Lampam Beach. People come to Phatthalung for the quiet, the nature, and honest local food.
bestTime: December–April, clear skies — Thale Noi is bright and the red lotus bloom beautifully, and the mountains and waterfalls are pleasant. The heavy rains fall around October–December

highlights.name: Thale Noi and the Red Lotus
highlights.blurb: A freshwater lake and well-known wetland. Take a boat out to see the red lotus covering the water in the morning, plus flocks of waterbirds and water buffalo that wade in to graze across the lake. It's the first image that comes to mind when you think of Phatthalung.

highlights.name: Khao Ok Thalu
highlights.blurb: A limestone mountain in the middle of town with a hole straight through near its peak, which has become the province's symbol. Climb the stairs for views over the town and the surrounding rice fields. A troop of monkeys greets you at the foot of the hill.

highlights.name: Lampam Beach
highlights.blurb: A beach on Songkhla Lake where locals come to sit in the breeze and eat seafood by the water. There are piers and pavilions for watching the sunset — an easy spot to relax close to town.

highlights.name: The Governor's Residence and Old Town
highlights.blurb: Old houses and markets in town that still carry an old-world feel. The former governor's residence is open to walk through, along with wooden shophouses and local food shops nearby.

highlights.name: Shadow Puppetry and Manora Dance
highlights.blurb: Phatthalung is a major birthplace of nang talung shadow puppetry and Manora dance in the South. You can visit the homes of puppet masters and Manora troupes to watch the puppets being carved and the dancing — folk arts that are still very much alive.

highlights.name: Rice Fields and Lakeside Buffalo Life
highlights.blurb: Green rice fields around town and water buffalo raised along the lake are everyday scenes you'll see across the province. Several spots set up rice paddies for photos and let you taste local Sangyod rice.

foodScene.name: Khao Yam (Southern Rice Salad)
foodScene.note: Rice tossed with budu sauce, finely shredded vegetables, toasted coconut, dried shrimp, and wild flowers — sour, salty, and sweet in one plate. A light breakfast that people in Phatthalung eat regularly.

foodScene.name: Gaeng Tai Pla and Khua Kling
foodScene.note: Bold local southern dishes. Gaeng tai pla is a rich, salty, spicy fish-innards curry, while khua kling is fragrant dry-fried minced pork with curry paste — eaten with hot rice and a big pile of fresh raw vegetables.

foodScene.name: Khanom Jeen with Southern Curry
foodScene.note: A popular breakfast — fresh rice noodles topped with bold southern curry, nam prik, and gaeng tai pla, with all the raw vegetables you want. The well-known shops in town open early and draw a queue.

foodScene.name: Lake Seafood and Pla Duk Ra
foodScene.note: On Songkhla Lake there's brackish-water fish and fresh prawns. The shops along Lampam Beach boil, stir-fry, and deep-fry it, while fried pla duk ra (salted catfish) is a local specialty that pairs well with rice porridge.

foodScene.name: Phatthalung Sangyod Rice
foodScene.note: The province's red heirloom rice, registered as a geographical indication. Cooked, it's fragrant and soft; it's sold as raw grain and turned into sweets and souvenirs.

foodScene.name: Southern Rice and Curry
foodScene.note: Curry shops line up trays of dishes ladled over a single plate of rice — gaeng leuang, gaeng tai pla, spicy stir-fries, and khua kling, all bold and properly southern. Found all over town.

foodScene.name: Roti and Southern-Style Cha Chak
foodScene.note: Southern tea shops open from morning to late night. Roti is crisp outside and soft inside, eaten with condensed milk or curry, alongside hot pulled tea (cha chak) — a breakfast and snack for sitting and chatting.

foodScene.name: Cafes with Rice-Field and Mountain Views
foodScene.note: Around town and along the fields are new cafes where you can sit looking out at the rice paddies and Khao Ok Thalu. Many brew fresh coffee and make local sweets — a good spot to relax and take photos.

attractions.name: Thale Noi Waterfowl Park
attractions.blurb: A wetland and lake where you take a boat to see red lotus blooming in the morning, many kinds of waterbirds, and water buffalo out in the lake. It's the nature spot people associate most with Phatthalung.

attractions.name: Khao Ok Thalu
attractions.blurb: A mountain in the center of town with a hole through its peak, the province's symbol. Climb the stairs for views over the town and rice fields; the foot of the hill has a troop of monkeys and an old temple.

attractions.name: Lampam Beach
attractions.blurb: A beach on Songkhla Lake where people sit in the breeze, eat seafood by the water, and watch the sunset. There are piers and lakeside pavilions for an easy rest.

attractions.name: Khao Pu–Khao Ya Forest Park
attractions.blurb: Forested hills in the Banthat range with caves, waterfalls, and short trails. The air is cool and pleasant — a good stop for a swim and some nature when you want to escape town.

attractions.name: Phrai Wan Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A waterfall in the Banthat forest with several tiers and clear, cool water. A short walk takes you in to swim and have a meal by the falls — a popular nature spot in the province.

attractions.name: Phatthalung Governor's Residence
attractions.blurb: The preserved old wooden home of Phatthalung's former governors, open to walk through. You can see the architecture and household items from the old days — a place to learn the town's history.

attractions.name: Wat Khian Bang Kaeo
attractions.blurb: An ancient temple long tied to Phatthalung, with an old stupa and a museum of local artifacts. It's a center of faith and a trace of the province's history.

attractions.name: Waterfowl Park and Ekkachai Bridge
attractions.blurb: A long bridge route across Thale Noi where you can drive or cycle for wide views of the lake and lotus fields. It's a popular photo stop before boarding a boat to see the birds.
